rules: All holder dictionaries below are copied exactly from accepted C01 research (japan.json). Grouping them under an existing person ID does not promote dates, prove a tenure or extend an office.
Only c01_accepted observations (C01-29, C01-31) qualify a person or a window. C01-12 Prime Minister observations are integrated but historically pending and are listed as not relied on.

Point observations are never expanded to full terms. No start or end is inferred from a successor, election, convention, resignation intent, retrospective or continuation statement; those remain claims.

Requested windows are appearance intervals from the CLAUDE-C06-JAPAN-01 handoff with exclusive ends, built from leadership-production required windows. Where a bound comes from party_leaders.json or leadership production rather than accepted research, the person entry says so.
Real history stops at 2026-09-07; every window in this batch lies before it.

Image dates describe the source image, never the appearance window. An unknown capture date stays unknown. Page copyright notices, later archive captures and editing or PDF-creation metadata are recorded separately and do not establish hard capture deadlines. Artistic ageing and body/clothing extensions are disclosed.

Likeness references identify the exact person and preserve the stated source licence and original bytes. The independent review permits the documented licensed official Yamahana film frame. Murayama and Ota use undated official portraits with illustrative ageing; neither has a proved capture deadline. Registration and output review remain future work.

Claude generates, edits and labels no image. Codex renders with its built-in image tool from the exact prompt files and input order in render-request-batch-01.md and returns the unchanged outputs; Claude then performs and records the identity, likeness, era and visual review. No review flag is true yet.
Each review batch contains at most ten people.
HTTP response header captures, and any response body that contains the client IP address or GeoIP data, are never copied, cited, hashed or committed.

Prompt sha256 values are over the LF bytes committed to Git (equal to `git show HEAD:<path> | sha256sum`). No .gitattributes rule covers these files yet, so a Windows checkout with core.autocrlf=true writes CRLF bytes; that hash is recorded beside each pin.
Birth dates used for age notes are general biographical knowledge, not accepted C01 research (Murayama's comes from the Kantei page).

Tracked repository inputs (research, receipts, registry, manifest, style anchor) are pinned by their committed blob bytes, so the pins hold on any checkout; where this Windows checkout writes CRLF, the entry says so.
